messages.subject: mixed effects analysis in R
parts:
I need to analyze a biological experiment where cell cultures are
grown at two different conditions, there are 4 "biological" replicates
of each, and 3-4 "technical" replicates. Biological replicates are
separate batches of cell culture grown from scratch under the same
condition; technical replicates are repeated measurements on the same
batch of cell culture. I need to determine if there's a significant
difference between the outcomes of the two growth conditions and how
the differences between the biological replicates compare to the
measurement errors. Is there an accessible tutorial on how to tackle
this? I've looked at the MASS book, but I find it too terse and hard
to read for somebody who is not a professional statistician. Also,
looks like R has at least 2 packages for mixed models: nlme and lme4.
Is there an advantage in using one vs the other?

Thanks.

Yury

lme4 was created after nlme and reflects more recent developments in
the theory and computational methods so I would recommend that
package. I co-authored both of those packages and would be happy to
talk with you about fitting models with them if you wish (and if you
are in Madison).
